title: Author + implement PROP-083: forensically diagnose why PROP-080 pre-push hook missed 17 post-deploy decider closures; ship the actual fix once root cause is confirmed; bulk-grandfather the 937 pre-deploy historical entries + the 17 post-deploy entries
background:
Today's 01:18Z integrity audit fired ISS-2621 (critical): 'Mech-A-bypass false-closures: 18 decider-self-apply entries lack verification_pattern (PROP-059)'. Operator inspection 06:00Z found the violations break down as:

  - **937 pre-PROP-080-deploy** (deploy was 2026-06-06T05:43Z) — historical sunk-cost; were never protected by the hook because the hook didn't exist yet. Bulk-grandfather candidates per the PROP-076 retroactive-annotation pattern.
  - **17 post-PROP-080-deploy** — THE REAL BUG. PROP-080's pre-push hook should have blocked each push that included one of these closures. It did not.

Sample post-deploy violations, all from 2026-06-06 decider runs:

  ISS-2619  2026-06-06T17:11:12  decider-self-apply-FAIL-019-schema-rename
  ISS-2620  2026-06-06T17:10:39  decider-self-apply-tracker-archive-move
  ISS-2609  2026-06-06T17:09:51  decider-self-apply-c4-h3
  ISS-2610  2026-06-06T17:09:51  decider-self-apply-c4-h4
  ISS-2611  2026-06-06T17:09:51  decider-self-apply-c4-h5
  ISS-2612  2026-06-06T17:09:51  decider-self-apply-c4-h6
  ISS-2613  2026-06-06T17:09:51  decider-self-apply-c3-h1
  ISS-2614  2026-06-06T17:09:51  decider-self-apply-c3-h2

  (...9 more from the same and subsequent decider runs)

The fixed_at clustering (six entries at exactly 17:09:51) shows decider closed 6+ ISSs in one run and pushed; the hook either didn't fire or fired without blocking.

**OPERATOR HYPOTHESIS (TO VERIFY OR DISPROVE — NOT TO ASSUME):**

The hook only gets installed on initial clone-creation, not on clone-reuse. PROP-080's diff put the `cat > .git/hooks/pre-push <<HOOK` block right after the clone-creation step. Decider's prompt typically uses `if [ ! -d "$CLONE" ]; then git clone ... fi` — so when subsequent runs find an existing clone, the conditional skips and the hook never gets re-installed. Decider's FIRST run after PROP-080 deploy probably worked (initial clone installed hook). All later runs that day reused the existing clone — no hook.

This is operator's THIRD hypothesis-from-current-state-inspection in 5 days. The last two were both wrong (PROP-077 H5, PROP-079 timeline correction) — tinker's forensic replay disproved them. Tinker should treat this hypothesis as a STARTING POINT for forensics, NOT a confirmed diagnosis. Replay the 2026-06-06T17:09:51 decider run trail and verify what actually happened.

**CANDIDATE ALTERNATIVE HYPOTHESES**:

  H1 (operator's): hook-install only on clone-creation, skipped on clone-reuse.
  H2: hook IS installed but exits 0 due to a filter bug (e.g., the exception list in lint-close-records.js matches decider-self-apply-c4-h3 somehow).
  H3: decider pushed via push-via-api.js fallback, which bypasses git hooks; PROP-080's diff DID patch the API path but maybe the patch has a hole.
  H4: decider used `git push --no-verify` somewhere (would skip the hook entirely).
  H5: hook is installed but a tier-related permissions issue prevents exec (e.g., chmod +x didn't actually fire because of sandbox).
  H6: 5+ pushes happened in the 17:09:51 window from multiple agent instances; one had the hook, others didn't, and origin/main only reflects the unhooked push.

Tinker's forensic toolkit (proven on PROP-077 H5 and PROP-079 timeline): md5 the lint script in the decider commit trees, replay the filter against the violating entries, check the prompt-text presence, check for the hook's presence in each commit tree's .git directory if accessible, audit the push-via-api.js code path.

operator_decision.approve_investigate_then_fix: YES — but with explicit instruction to forensically verify the actual root cause BEFORE implementing. The operator's hypothesis H1 might be wrong (it has been twice already this week). Once tinker confirms the dominant failure mode (H1 or one of H2-H6 or H7-new), implement the structural fix matching the confirmed cause.
operator_decision.rationale: PROP-080 was supposed to be the proof-of-concept of structural enforcement. If it has a hole, every meta-pattern fix (PROP-081, PROP-082) is suspect by inheritance. Critical to nail the actual root cause.

requested_work:
Step 1 — Forensic diagnosis (THE CRITICAL STEP). For the 2026-06-06T17:09:51 decider run that closed 6+ ISSs:
  (a) Find the decider commit SHA that landed those closures on origin/main.
  (b) From that commit's tree, check whether `.git/hooks/pre-push` would have been installed by walking the decider prompt's clone-setup code path: was the hook-install block UNCONDITIONAL or conditional on `if [ ! -d "$CLONE" ]`?
  (c) Replay `lint-close-records.js` (md5-verified identical to current) against the commit's added closed-issues.json entries; confirm all 6+ would have triggered exit-1 if the hook had run.
  (d) Check whether the push went via plain git or via `monitor/scripts/push-via-api.js`. Inspect the run report or stdout if surviving.
  (e) Rule in/out each of H1-H6 from the directive's hypothesis list. Be explicit about WHICH hypothesis is the dominant failure mode (may be more than one).
  (f) If a NEW hypothesis (H7+) emerges from forensics, document it and treat it as the dominant cause. The operator's H1 is a starting point, NOT a confirmed diagnosis.

Step 2 — Author monitor/tinker/proposals/PROP-083-prop080-hook-persistence-fix.json. Required sections: title, problem statement (cite this directive + ISS-2621 + the post-deploy violations + tinker's Step 1 forensics), DOMINANT FAILURE MODE (with evidence + which alternative hypotheses were ruled out), proposed fix matching the actual root cause, Q-OPs if any, verification_pattern, files_touched, estimated_loc.

Step 3 — Operator pre-approves the following IF the dominant failure mode is one of these (tinker picks the matching fix):
  - If H1 (hook-install on clone-creation only): make hook installation IDEMPOTENT — install on every cycle if missing, regardless of clone-create vs reuse. Pattern: `[ -x .git/hooks/pre-push ] || (cat > ... && chmod +x)`. Cheap, structural, safe to re-run.
  - If H2 (filter bug): tighten the filter logic in lint-close-records.js to match the exact bypass case.
  - If H3 (push-via-api.js path bug): patch the API path's lint-invocation properly so it fires before the API push.
  - If H4 (--no-verify): grep all prompts + scripts for --no-verify and remove. Add a CLAUDE.md prohibition.
  - If H5 (exec/permissions): add a sanity-check that the hook is exec'able before push.
  - If H6 (concurrent pushes): rate-limit or serialize decider's push step.
  - If H7+ (new): tinker uses judgment + operator-approval-if-needed for novel fixes.

Step 4 — Bulk-grandfather the 937 pre-PROP-080-deploy entries. Mirror the PROP-076 retroactive-annotation pattern: set `audit_grandfathered = 'PROP-080-pre-deploy historical sunk-cost; structural enforcement landed 2026-06-06T05:43Z, these closures predate it'` (or similar concise reason). Bulk-update in closed-issues.json. Operator pre-approves this annotation pattern verbatim.

Step 5 — Bulk-grandfather the 17 post-PROP-080-deploy entries. Reason: `'PROP-080 hook-persistence-gap, fix landing as PROP-083; closure_reason validates the underlying patch is present in target file'` (or similar — adjust to whatever the actual H-confirmed root cause is). Operator pre-approves the annotation; the underlying work is correct, only the discipline-tracking was bypassed.

Step 6 — Tinker self-applies the prompt + script edits per the PROP-076/077/078/079/080/081/082 pattern: write proposal, implement same run if total LOC <100, verification pattern passes (grep + simulation showing the fix would have caught the 17 violations).

Step 7 — Validation: simulate the next decider run after PROP-083 deploys. The hook (or whatever the fix is) should fire on EVERY run, not just clone-creation cycles. Document simulation outcomes in PROP-083's verification section.

Step 8 — Close ISS-2621 with closure_resolution citing PROP-083 + this directive + the grandfather pattern. The 17 + 937 entries are now properly annotated, so integrity's next run will not re-fire the critical.

Step 9 — Lifecycle: flip PROP-083.json status='implemented' with implementation_commit/at/run. Flip this directive to status='completed' with prop_id_implemented set. Update PROP-080's status note to reference PROP-083 as the hook-persistence fix (do NOT supersede PROP-080 — it remains canonical for the gate; PROP-083 just hardens the install).

Step 10 — Manually copy edited prompt + script files to FUSE so decider's next session-bootstrap picks up the new hook-install logic. dome-mirror will propagate within ~30 min but manual sync is the safe bootstrap path.

Do NOT change PROP-080's filter logic in lint-close-records.js unless Step 1 confirms a filter bug. The filter is the canonical spec; bypass investigation is the work here.
Do NOT broaden scope to other decider close-paths beyond the close-record write. Stay focused on the hook persistence (or whatever H-confirmed root cause is) for the PROP-080 gate.

Do NOT attempt to retroactively determine which of the 17 post-deploy closures were 'real fixes' vs 'gaps'. Operator pre-approves bulk-grandfather all 17; the underlying patches are presumed correct per integrity's spot-checks pattern (matches the PROP-076 sunk-cost grandfather pattern).
Do NOT supersede PROP-080. It remains the canonical filter + gate spec. PROP-083 is a persistence hardening; analogous to how PROP-077 Part A was defense-in-depth and PROP-078 was the structural fix.

Do NOT touch DIRECTIVE-20260607-001 (the prune↔workspace-sync loop fix) or its outputs. The two directives are orthogonal; tinker may dispatch in either order based on priority — operator will manually fire tinker after BOTH directives land.
